'''Sheheen''': {{legend0|#a5b0ff|40–50%}} {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} {{legend0|#6674de|60–70%}} {{legend0|#584cde|70–80%}} {{legend0|#3933e5|80–90%}} {{legend0|#0d0596|>90%}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Mark Sanford]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Nikki Haley]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsSC}} The '''2010 South Carolina gubernatorial election''' took place on November 2, 2010. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Governor of South Carolina|Governor]] [[Mark Sanford]] was [[term limits in the United States|term-limited]] and unable to seek re-election. [[Partisan primary|Primary election]]s took place on June 8, 2010, and a [[Two-round system|runoff election]], as was necessary on the Republican side, was held two weeks later on June 22. Republican [[Nikki Haley]] defeated Democrat [[Vincent Sheheen]] in the general election by a margin of 4.5%. As of 2023, this is the closest that the Democrats have come to winning the governorship of South Carolina since their last victory in [[1998 South Carolina gubernatorial election|1998]]. This is the first open-seat election since [[1994 South Carolina gubernatorial election|1994]]. Haley was re-elected in [[2014 South Carolina gubernatorial election|2014]] in a rematch with Sheheen. ==Republican primary== According to [[CNN]], Haley initially entered the gubernatorial primary as a [[dark horse]] candidate. In an article covering her surge in the primary in the weeks prior to the election, it was noted that a "surprise" endorsement from former Alaska governor and [[2008 United States presidential election|2008]] vice presidential candidate [[Sarah Palin]] boosted Haley's candidacy. Haley's campaign was backed by TV ads run by ReformSC, an advocacy group funded by allies of outgoing Governor [[Mark Sanford]].{{Cite web |last=Hamby |first=Peter |date=May 20, 2010 |title=Haley has momentum in South Carolina race, rivals admit |url=https://politicalticker.blogs.cnn.com/2010/05/20/haley-has-momentum-in-south-carolina-race-rivals-admit/ |access-date=February 8, 2023 |website=CNN |language=en |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100523235726/https://politicalticker.blogs.cnn.com/2010/05/20/haley-has-momentum-in-south-carolina-race-rivals-admit/ |archive-date=May 23, 2010 |url-status=dead}} ===Candidates=== *[[Gresham Barrett]], [[South Carolina's 3rd congressional district|U.S. representative]][http://www.thestate.com/154/story/702819.html Barrett running for S.C. governor] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090305225428/http://www.thestate.com/154/story/702819.html |date=2009-03-05 }} The State, Mar. 4, 2009 *[[André Bauer]], [[Lieutenant Governor of South Carolina|lieutenant governor]][http://www.carolinalive.com/news/story.aspx?id=369789 Lt Gov Bauer makes run for governor official] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722212806/http://www.carolinalive.com/news/story.aspx?id=369789 |date=2011-07-22 }} WPDE, Oct. 29, 2009 *[[Nikki Haley]], [[South Carolina House of Representatives|state representative]][http://www.thestate.com/breaking/story/786616.html Haley announces run for governor] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20130205034916/http://www.thestate.com/breaking/story/786616.html |date=2013-02-05 }} The State, May 14, 2009 *[[Henry McMaster]], [[Attorney General of South Carolina|state attorney general]][http://www2.counton2.com/cbd/news/local/article/henry_mcmaster_seeking_s.c._governor_post/49952/ Henry McMaster seeking S.C.
